groups.label: Intensity
groups.hint: Scale the effect by these factors.

groups.label: Composite signal noise
groups.hint: Noise applied to the composite NTSC signal.

groups.label: Head switching
groups.hint: Emulate VHS head-switching artifacts at the bottom of the image.

groups.label: Start mid-line
groups.hint: Start the head-switching artifact mid-scanline, with some static where it begins.

groups.label: Tracking noise
groups.hint: Emulate noise from VHS tracking error.

groups.label: Ringing
groups.hint: Additional ringing artifacts, simulated with a notch filter.

groups.label: Luma noise
groups.hint: Noise applied to the luminance signal. Useful for higher-frequency noise than the "Composite noise" setting can provide.

groups.label: Chroma noise
groups.hint: Noise applied to the chrominance (color) signal.

groups.label: Chroma distortion
groups.hint: Phase and delay errors in the color subcarrier.

groups.label: Sharpen
groups.hint: Sharpening of the image, as done by some VHS decks.

params.label: Crop
params.hint: Crop the picture to an aspect ratio before anything else in the chain sees it.

params.label: Position left – right
params.hint: Where the crop sits wherever there's room: 0 the left edge, 1 the right, 0.5 the middle.

params.label: Position top – bottom
params.hint: Where the crop sits wherever there's room: 0 the top edge, 1 the bottom, 0.5 the middle.

params.label: Zoom
params.hint: 1: the largest crop for the ratio; more zooms in (2: half its width and height).

params.label: Downscale before shader
params.hint: Reduce the picture to a retro horizontal resolution before the shader; the height follows the source's aspect ratio.

params.label: Horizontal resolution
params.hint: Console preset: sets the width. Purely a label otherwise ("Custom" when the width is edited).

params.label: Width
params.hint: Horizontal resolution in pixels. Height follows the source's aspect ratio.

params.label: Sampling
params.hint: Chunky takes one source pixel per block — hard pixel edges (on detailed video they can shimmer). Smooth averages the whole block — softer, steady.

params.label: Digital video
params.hint: A small video codec run for real: capture, 8×8 DCT blocks or Microsoft Video 1's 4×4 color blocks, quantization, motion-compensated prediction, data loss.

params.label: Codec
params.hint: How the picture is compressed. DCT, the MPEG, H.263 and DV family, blurs detail inside 8×8 blocks and rings around edges. Block colors is Microsoft Video 1 (1992, Video for Windows): each 4×4 block becomes one, two or eight flat 15-bit colors and unchanged blocks are skipped — chunky two-tone edges and banded gradients, the early CD-ROM look.

params.label: Color
params.hint: How much color detail is kept against brightness detail. Codecs store color at lower resolution because eyes notice it less: 4:2:2 halves it across, 4:2:0 across and down, and 4:1:1, NTSC DV's choice, quarters it across, smearing color sideways.

params.label: Quality
params.hint: How finely each 8×8 block's detail is kept (the quantizer). Lower turns blocks into flat tiles and rings edges with mosquito noise.

params.label: Quality (from 0.4.0)
params.hint: This instance was made with NTSCRT 0.4.0, whose Quality slider ran on JPEG's own curve. While Quality above is at its default, this value (converted to the same quantizer) is used instead. Set it to 0 to drop it.

params.label: Keyframe interval
params.hint: Seconds between keyframes (whole pictures). Between them the codec only sends what moved, so errors and datamoshing persist until the next one. 0 compresses every frame on its own, like Motion JPEG and DV.

params.label: Fixed bitrate
params.hint: How strictly the codec keeps to a fixed bitrate. Busy frames — motion, detail, grain — have to share the same bits, so they turn blocky, and the picture sharpens again when things settle.

params.label: Deblocking
params.hint: The decoder smoothing block edges, as H.264 does. Off keeps the hard tiles of older codecs; on trades them for smear.

params.label: Frame rate
params.hint: How many pictures a second the camera captures. Below the clip's own rate, frames repeat — the stutter of old webcams and video calls.

params.label: Fields
params.hint: Interlaced cameras like the VX1000 record each frame as two fields of alternate lines. One field keeps just one, as most DV reached the web: the CRT gets half as many lines, each twice as tall, and draws a scanline per line — the 240p look — while anywhere without the CRT each line shows twice, turning diagonals to stairs.

params.label: Aliasing
params.hint: The sensor reading detail it can't resolve, with nothing blurring it away first: fine stripes beat into moiré and edges into jaggies. Red, green and blue are sampled a third of a pixel apart, so where a beat drifts slowly its colors cycle through the rainbow. Above 50% the finest detail is boosted as it's read, for stronger moiré from sources not much sharper than the camera.

params.label: Lens softness (removed)
params.hint: From NTSCRT 0.4.0. Lens softness is gone (upstream 0.19); kept so older projects load. No effect.

params.label: Sensor noise
params.hint: Grain from a small, cheap image sensor, strongest in the color. It changes every frame, so the codec spends its bits on it and blocks crawl in flat areas.

params.label: Noise reduction
params.hint: The camera smoothing its own grain away before compressing. It flattens fine detail into a smeary, plastic look.

params.label: CCD response
params.hint: The tone of a 90s 3-CCD camcorder like the VX1000, fitted to its footage. Auto exposure meters the middle of the frame and exposes bright; each color is compressed by the knee and then clips at white on its own, so warm skin and skies go yellow, then white; lens flare and the mishandled 7.5 IRE setup lift the blacks to a milky gray, more in bright scenes. 0% leaves the picture alone.

params.label: Exposure (from 0.4.0)
params.hint: This instance was made with NTSCRT 0.4.0, whose Exposure became CCD response. While CCD response is 0 it sets CCD response (the stronger of this and Black level decides). Set it to 0 to drop it.

params.label: Black level (from 0.4.0)
params.hint: This instance was made with NTSCRT 0.4.0, whose Black level became CCD response. While CCD response is 0 it sets CCD response (the stronger of this and Exposure decides). Set it to 0 to drop it.

params.label: White balance
params.hint: Warm (positive) or cool (negative): the camera's guess at the light, often wrong.

params.label: Tint
params.hint: Magenta (positive) or green (negative), the other way a camera's color can drift.

params.label: Saturation
params.hint: Color strength. Consumer camcorders pushed it, reds and oranges most visibly.

params.label: Sharpening
params.hint: The camera's detail circuit: edges get bright and dark outlines (halos), the crisp, hard-edged video look.

params.label: Data loss
params.hint: Lost packets or tape dropouts. The decoder patches the gap from the last picture it had. Every frame on its own (DV), the patches flash and vanish; between keyframes, they smear and drift until the next keyframe.

params.label: Datamosh
params.hint: Keyframes thrown away. The changes that follow are applied to the old picture instead of the new one: motion drags the previous scene's pixels around until a keyframe gets through. Needs a keyframe interval above 0.

params.label: NTSC signal
params.hint: ntsc-rs analog signal simulation (composite / VHS).

params.label: Intensity
params.hint: Scale the effect by these factors.

params.label: Horizontal intensity
params.hint: Horizontally scale the effect by this amount. For 480p video, leave this at 1.0 for the most physically-accurate result.

params.label: Vertical intensity
params.hint: Vertically scale the effect by this amount. You should probably leave this at 1.0.

params.label: Scale with video size
params.hint: Multiply the scaling factors by the video's height. Prefer scaling the input video to 480p instead, which gives much more accurate-looking results.

params.label: Use field
params.hint: Choose which rows ("fields" in NTSC parlance) of the source image will be used.

options.label: Alternating
options.hint: Skip every other row, alternating between skipping even and odd rows.

options.label: Upper only
options.hint: Skip every lower row, keeping the upper ones.

options.label: Lower only
options.hint: Skip every upper row, keeping the lower ones.

options.label: Interleaved (upper first)
options.hint: Treat the video as interlaced, with the upper field as the earlier frame.

options.label: Interleaved (lower first)
options.hint: Treat the video as interlaced, with the lower field as the earlier frame.

options.label: Both
options.hint: Use all rows; don't skip any.

params.label: Lowpass filter type
params.hint: The low-pass filter to use throughout the effect.

options.label: Constant K (blurry)
options.hint: Simple constant-k filter. Produces longer, blurry results.

options.label: Butterworth (sharper)
options.hint: Filter with a sharper falloff. Produces sharpened, less blurry results.

params.label: Input luma filter
params.hint: Filter the input luminance to decrease rainbow artifacts.

options.label: Notch
options.hint: Apply a notch filter to the input luminance signal. Sharp, but has ringing artifacts.

options.label: Box
options.hint: Apply a simple box filter to the input luminance signal.

options.label: None
options.hint: Do not filter the luminance signal. Adds rainbow artifacts.

params.label: Chroma low-pass in
params.hint: Apply a low-pass filter to the input chrominance (color) signal.

options.label: Full
options.hint: Full-intensity low-pass filter.

options.label: Light
options.hint: Less intense low-pass filter.

options.label: None
options.hint: No low-pass filter.

params.label: Composite signal sharpening
params.hint: Boost high frequencies in the NTSC signal, sharpening the image and intensifying colors.

params.label: Composite signal noise
params.hint: Noise applied to the composite NTSC signal.

params.label: Intensity
params.hint: Intensity of the noise.

params.label: Frequency
params.hint: Base wavelength, in pixels, of the noise.

params.label: Detail
params.hint: Octaves of noise.

params.label: Snow
params.hint: Frequency of random speckles in the image.

params.label: Snow anisotropy
params.hint: Determines whether the speckles are placed truly randomly or concentrated in certain rows.

params.label: Scanline phase shift
params.hint: Phase shift of the chrominance (color) signal each scanline. Usually 180 degrees.

params.label: Chroma demodulation filter
params.hint: Filter used to modulate the chrominance (color) data out of the composite NTSC signal.

options.label: Box
options.hint: Simple horizontal box blur.

options.label: Notch
options.hint: Notch filter. Sharper than a box blur, but with ringing artifacts.

options.label: 1-line comb
options.hint: Average the current row with the previous one, phase-cancelling the chrominance (color) signals. Only works if the scanline phase shift is 180 degrees.

options.label: 2-line comb
options.hint: Average the current row with the previous and next ones, phase-cancelling the chrominance (color) signals. Only works if the scanline phase shift is 180 degrees.

params.label: Head switching
params.hint: Emulate VHS head-switching artifacts at the bottom of the image.

params.label: Height
params.hint: Total height of the head-switching artifact.

params.label: Offset
params.hint: How much of the head-switching artifact is off-screen.

params.label: Horizontal shift
params.hint: How much the head-switching artifact shifts rows horizontally.

params.label: Start mid-line
params.hint: Start the head-switching artifact mid-scanline, with some static where it begins.

params.label: Position
params.hint: Horizontal position at which the head-switching starts.

params.label: Jitter
params.hint: How much the head-switching artifact "jitters" horizontally.

params.label: Tracking noise
params.hint: Emulate noise from VHS tracking error.

params.label: Height
params.hint: Total height of the tracking artifacts.

params.label: Wave intensity
params.hint: How much the affected scanlines "wave" back and forth.

params.label: Snow intensity
params.hint: Frequency of speckle-type noise in the artifacts.

params.label: Snow anisotropy
params.hint: How much the speckles are clustered by scanline.

params.label: Noise intensity
params.hint: Intensity of non-speckle noise.

params.label: Ringing
params.hint: Additional ringing artifacts, simulated with a notch filter.

params.label: Frequency
params.hint: Frequency/period of the ringing, in "rings per pixel".

params.label: Power
params.hint: The power of the notch filter / how far out the ringing extends.

params.label: Scale
params.hint: Intensity of the ringing.

params.label: Luma noise
params.hint: Noise applied to the luminance signal. Useful for higher-frequency noise than the "Composite noise" setting can provide.

params.label: Intensity
params.hint: Intensity of the noise.

params.label: Frequency
params.hint: Base wavelength, in pixels, of the noise.

params.label: Detail
params.hint: Octaves of noise.

params.label: Chroma noise
params.hint: Noise applied to the chrominance (color) signal.

params.label: Intensity
params.hint: Intensity of the noise.

params.label: Frequency
params.hint: Base wavelength, in pixels, of the noise.

params.label: Detail
params.hint: Octaves of noise.

params.label: Chroma phase error
params.hint: Phase error for the chrominance (color) signal.

params.label: Chroma phase noise
params.hint: Noise applied per-scanline to the phase of the chrominance (color) signal.

params.label: Chroma delay (horizontal)
params.hint: Horizontal offset of the chrominance (color) signal.

params.label: Chroma delay (vertical)
params.hint: Vertical offset of the chrominance (color) signal. Usually increases with VHS generation loss.

params.label: Tape speed
params.hint: Emulate cutoff of high-frequency data at various VHS recording speeds.

params.label: Chroma loss
params.hint: Chance that the chrominance (color) signal is completely lost in each scanline.

params.label: Sharpen
params.hint: Sharpening of the image, as done by some VHS decks.

params.label: Intensity
params.hint: Amount of sharpening to apply.

params.label: Frequency
params.hint: Frequency / radius of the sharpening, relative to the tape speed's cutoff frequency.

params.label: Edge wave
params.hint: Horizontal waving of the image.

params.label: Intensity
params.hint: Horizontal waving of the image, in pixels.

params.label: Speed
params.hint: Speed at which the horizontal waving occurs.

params.label: Frequency
params.hint: Base wavelength for the horizontal waving.

params.label: Detail
params.hint: Octaves of noise for the waves.

params.label: Vertically blend chroma
params.hint: Vertically blend each scanline's chrominance with the scanline above it.

params.label: Chroma low-pass out
params.hint: Apply a low-pass filter to the output chroma signal.

options.label: Full
options.hint: Full-intensity low-pass filter.

options.label: Light
options.hint: Less intense low-pass filter.

options.label: None
options.hint: No low-pass filter.

params.label: Glitch
params.hint: TV receiver and VCR transport simulation. Defaults describe a healthy set: enabling changes nothing until a knob is turned.

params.label: Signal strength
params.hint: Antenna signal level. Lowering it brings snow first, then flickering and lost color as the color burst drowns, then broken sync as the sync pulses do — the order a real set fails in.

params.label: Vertical hold
params.hint: The vertical oscillator's free-running speed. Near the center the sync pulses pull it into lock; past the lock range the picture rolls, with the blanking bar crossing the screen.

params.label: Horizontal hold
params.hint: The horizontal oscillator's free-running speed. Off center the picture slides sideways as the AFC strains to hold it; further and lock breaks — the picture tears into diagonal bands and the color goes wild.

params.label: AFC response
params.hint: How quickly the TV's horizontal AFC follows timing changes. Slow sets ride out noise but bend at the top of the picture on VCR playback (flagging); fast ones track tape timing but jitter in noise.

params.label: Brightness
params.hint: Raises the picture tube's black level, as turning up a TV's brightness did. The blanking intervals and sync pulses become visible when the picture rolls or tears.

params.label: Ghost
params.hint: A reflected copy of the signal arriving late (multipath). Negative values invert it, as reflections often did. Its color shifts with the delay, because the delayed color carrier arrives at a different phase.

params.label: Ghost delay
params.hint: How late the reflection arrives. 1 µs is about 2% of the picture width — a reflection path roughly 300 m longer than the direct one.

params.label: Hum
params.hint: Mains hum leaking into the video: light and dark bars that drift slowly up the picture (60 Hz hum against the 59.94 Hz color field rate), bending the picture where the sync separator is pulled off.

params.label: Caption data
params.hint: Line 21 carries closed-caption data — the row of dashes visible in the blanking bar when the picture rolls.

params.label: Head switching
params.hint: Timing jump when the VCR changes heads, just before vertical sync. The bottom lines jump sideways and the TV's AFC chases the jump into the top of the next field — the bend called flagging.

params.label: Time-base jitter
params.hint: Tape stretch and transport flutter. The TV's AFC follows the slow wander; the fast jitter shows as ragged lines.

params.label: Tape crinkle
params.hint: Creased tape passing the heads: bands of signal loss and violent timing errors, enough to knock the TV out of lock for a moment.

params.label: Head clog
params.hint: Debris on the video heads, lifting them off the tape: whole fields drop out to noise and lose their sync, more often as the clog worsens.

params.label: Tracking error
params.hint: The heads drifting off the recorded tracks. Well tracked, the noise band where they cross to the next track rests in the vertical interval, out of sight; as the error grows it climbs into the picture and widens.

params.label: Search
params.hint: Fast-forward picture search. The spinning heads cross from track to track, reading noise between them: one fewer noise bar than the speed, drifting as the tracking phase slides, with the picture jumping at each crossing.

params.label: Dropouts
params.hint: Oxide missing from the tape: brief losses of signal, often a few lines tall. How they look depends on Dropout compensation.

params.label: Dropout compensation
params.hint: The VCR's fix for dropouts: replay the lost stretch from the line before. On, dropouts shrink to brief white ticks and short smears where one line repeats down a tall flaw; off, they show as long white streaks.

params.label: CRT shader
params.hint: Run the CRT shader chain (librashader). Off: the picture is scaled to the output without a shader.

params.label: LUT [ OFF, DARK BLUE, DARK BLUE (cool) ]
// Presets greater than 0 disable options with '*'.
Mask Preset [CUSTOM, APERT1, APERT2, SLOT1, SLOT2, DOT]
Screen Loop
params.hint: Video feedback: a camcorder pointed at the TV showing its own picture. Off = the host passes no feedback_json.

params.label: Zoom
params.hint: How big the TV's screen is in the camera's frame — each copy is this size of the one around it. Below 100% the copies shrink into a tunnel, more of them the closer you get to 100%. Above 100% every pass grows instead, into the swirling patterns feedback is known for. 0% points the camera away from the TV.

params.label: Vanishing point left – right
params.hint: Where the tunnel converges across the frame — the point the copies shrink toward (past 100% zoom, the point they grow away from). It stays put as you change the zoom and angles; the camera is re-aimed at the TV to keep it there. Set by the green dot on the preview.

params.label: Vanishing point up – down
params.hint: Where the tunnel converges up and down the frame. Set by the green dot on the preview.

params.label: Roll
params.hint: The TV turned against the camera. Every pass turns the picture again, so the tunnel becomes a spiral.

params.label: Side angle
params.hint: The camera looking at the screen from one side, so the screen's far edge is narrower. Every pass skews the picture again. At high zoom a steep angle magnifies the near side of the screen enough that part of the picture smears outward instead of forming copies.

params.label: Vertical angle
params.hint: The camera looking at the screen from above or below.

params.label: Handheld
params.hint: The camera operator's hands: a slow sway with a little tremor. Every copy is one trip round the loop older than the one around it, so the tunnel follows the camera a moment late and snakes.

params.label: Random seed
params.hint: Picks the handheld motion. The same seed always moves the same way — so the draft matches the render, and motion you like can always be found again.

params.label: Drift left – right
params.hint: How far the vanishing point slides across the frame over the render, easing in and out. Set by the blue ring on the preview.

params.label: Drift up – down
params.hint: How far the vanishing point slides up or down over the render. Set by the blue ring on the preview.

params.label: Push
params.hint: Zooming in or out over the render, from the Zoom you set.

params.label: Spin
params.hint: Rolling the camera over the render, from the Roll you set.

params.label: Seamless loop
params.hint: The move goes out and comes back, and the shake repeats over the length — so the file loops without a jump. Made for GIFs.

params.label: Softness
params.hint: The camera's focus on the screen. A little softness on every pass melts the deep copies first; sharp focus keeps the moiré of the screen's dot pattern.

params.label: Screen brightness
params.hint: How bright the TV looks to the camera — the loop's gain. Below 100% the deep copies fade to black; above, they burn to white.

params.label: Contrast
params.hint: The TV's contrast as the camera sees it, applied again on every pass — so the deep copies get harsher (or flatter) than the outer ones.

params.label: Color drift
params.hint: The camera's white balance against the TV's color temperature. The tint compounds on every pass: cool turns the deep copies teal and blue, warm turns them orange.

params.label: Hue drift
params.hint: A tint error that turns the hue a little on every pass, so the tunnel cycles through the colors.

params.label: Auto exposure
params.hint: The camcorder's automatic exposure. It reacts to the brightness of its own picture a moment late, so the whole loop pulses.

params.label: Luma key
params.hint: A video mixer between the camera and the TV keys your picture over the camera's: its bright parts sit on top, and the feedback shows through the darker parts — so your subject stays solid while the tunnel trails around it. Turn it up to key in darker tones too. Off, the TV shows only what the camera sees.

params.label: Key the dark parts
params.hint: Key your picture's dark parts on top instead, with the feedback showing through the bright ones — for dark subjects on light backgrounds.

params.label: Delay
params.hint: How long one trip around the loop takes. Each copy is that much older than the one around it, so anything moving — the camera included — echoes down the tunnel.

params.label: Camcorder counter
params.hint: The camcorder's elapsed-time counter, burned into its picture — so it's filmed again with everything else and repeats down the tunnel.

params.label: Length
params.hint: How long the move (drift, push, spin, seamless loop) takes, in seconds. Upstream uses the clip's duration for video and this for stills; hosts may set it to the effect's duration.

params.label: Transparent areas
params.hint: For titles and clips that don't fill the frame. Clip to element: the effect stays inside the element's shape. Let effect spill: ghosting, smear and glow extend past the element and show as light over what's underneath (like a Screen blend). No difference on full-frame video.

digital_formats.name: Webcam (2005)
digital_formats.hint: 320 × 240, 15 fps, a noisy sensor, each frame compressed on its own.

digital_formats.name: Video call
digital_formats.hint: A squeezed bitrate and lost packets that smear until the next keyframe.

digital_formats.name: MiniDV
digital_formats.hint: The VX1000 skate-video look: one field line-doubled, hard sharpening, aliasing and color moiré, blown highlights, warm saturated color, gray blacks, color at a quarter width (4:1:1).

digital_formats.name: Early web video
digital_formats.hint: 240p streaming: few bits, coarse blocks, and keyframes that pump.

digital_formats.name: CD-ROM (Video 1)
digital_formats.hint: Video for Windows off a 90s CD-ROM: 240 wide, 12 fps, Microsoft Video 1's flat two-tone blocks and banded 15-bit color, a keyframe every 15 frames.

digital_formats.name: Datamosh
digital_formats.hint: Keyframes removed: motion drags the old picture around.
